title: A mixed-currency month takes a different builder that drops the reporting window from every sheet header and writes 0.00 where the screen writes —
evidence:
August 2026 holds one ILS invoice and one USD invoice, so `buildStyledMonthlyWorkbook` hits `if (currencies.length > 1) return base;` (src/lib/monthlyReport.ts:487) and the file comes from the plain base builder instead. Two consequences, both measured in out/exports/downloads/reports-aug-mixed__עסק-לדוגמה-report-2026-08.xlsx (14,861 bytes, 8 sheets) against out/exports/07-reports-aug.png taken in the same session:
(a) WINDOW. Every one of the eight sheets carries the subtitle `2026-08 · הופק 04.09.2026, 02:42` and the summary sheet says `חודש | 2026-08`. A single-currency month says `ספטמבר 2026 · 01.09.2026–30.09.2026`. The difference is the format strings themselves: he.ts:2919 `xlProducedAt: '{month} · הופק {at}'` interpolates the raw ISO key, he.ts:2922 `xlStyledSubtitle: '{label} · {from}–{to} · הופק {at}'` interpolates the localized label and the start and end dates. So the mixed-currency file never states the window it covers — only a machine key with no start or end date.
(b) ZERO WHERE THE SCREEN SAYS NOTHING. The screen tile reads `שולם החודש כנגד חשבוניות —` and the payments table reads `אין תשלומים בחודש זה`. The file's summary sheet writes `תשלומים כנגד חשבוניות | 0 | 0.00 | ILS` on row 13 and `תשלומים כנגד חשבוניות | 0 | 0.00 | USD` on row 18. The base builder's `line()` helper (monthlyReport.ts:340-352) always writes `sum(rows, …)`, which is 0 over an empty array. The styled branch is explicitly careful about exactly this — its own comment at monthlyReport.ts:491 reads "A missing value stays an empty cell — never 0 (constitution: אפס הוא גם טענה על המציאות)" — so the rule is enforced on the single-currency path and not on the mixed-currency one.
What DOES hold: the split itself is correct. Eight sheets — חשבוניות ILS / חשבוניות USD / תשלומים ILS / תשלומים USD / זיכויים ILS / זיכויים USD — one summary block per currency, and no combined row anywhere. Nothing is summed across currencies.
repro: Sign in as owner → /reports?month=2026-08 (a month with one ILS and one USD invoice) → read the tile `שולם החודש כנגד חשבוניות` (—) → click ייצוא Excel → open the file → sheet פרטי הדוח rows 13 and 18, and the subtitle on any sheet.
expected: The mixed-currency workbook states its window the way the single-currency one does (`אוגוסט 2026 · 01.08.2026–31.08.2026`), and a month with no payments leaves those money cells empty rather than claiming 0.00 in two currencies.
actual: Subtitle is the raw key `2026-08` with no date range on all 8 sheets; payments and credits are asserted as 0.00 ILS and 0.00 USD for a month in which none exist, while the screen for the same month shows —.

title: Severity raised: the bare 'סיכום רכישות מוצרים' link now yields a SEPTEMBER file from a JULY report screen, in two clicks
evidence:
Known finding: on /reports, switching the month updates every tile except the 'סיכום רכישות מוצרים' link, which stays bare. The severity has changed because the wrong month now leaves the building as a file.
Measured (out/exports/07-link-evidence.json): on `/reports?month=2026-07` the month picker reads `07`/`2026` and 18 invoice rows are shown; the link's href is exactly `/reports/products` with no parameters. Following it lands on `/reports/products` with date inputs `2026-09-01`/`2026-09-04` and the caption `19 מוצרים · 2026-09-01 עד 2026-09-04`. Clicking ייצוא Excel there produced `product-purchases-2026-09-01-2026-09-04.xlsx` (out/exports/downloads/products-followed-july-link__…, 8,675 bytes, 19 rows).
Root cause is two-sided, and 0312 reached neither side: src/pages/Reports.tsx:444 is `<Link className="link" to="/reports/products">`, and src/pages/ProductPurchaseSummary.tsx contains no useSearchParams / useParamState at all — its window is component state, so it cannot accept a window from the URL even if the link offered one. Confirmed by navigating directly to `/reports/products?from=2020-01-01&to=2020-01-31`, which still rendered `2026-09-01 / 2026-09-04`.
repro: owner → /reports → pick יולי 2026 → click 'סיכום רכישות מוצרים ←' → read the date inputs → click ייצוא Excel → read the filename and the subtitle in row 2.
expected: The link carries the selected month, or the products screen accepts from/to from the URL, so the file a manager exports after reading a July report is a July file.
actual: The link is bare, the products screen resets to the current month-to-date and cannot be told otherwise by URL, and the export is a September file. The file's own header is honest (`01.09.2026 – 04.09.2026`); the user is the one misled.

title: 'No data' leaves the screen as — and reaches the file as three different things: a blank cell, a literal 0, and an em dash — sometimes all three in one workbook
evidence:
The constitution's rule is that a metric with no data shows — and never 0, because zero is a claim about reality. The exports break the rule three ways:
(1) /reports/products, product-purchases-2026-01-01-2026-12-31.xlsx: 115 data rows. `התקבל` is an EMPTY cell in 74 of them, `הוצאה ברוטו` is an EMPTY cell in all 115 — and the screen shows — in exactly those positions (out/exports/02-products-default.png, read). Raw XML for row 5: `<c r="D5" s="4"/><c r="E5" s="4"/>` … `<c r="K5" s="4"/>`, truly empty. Yet `מחיר יחידה ממוצע` in the SAME row is the shared string `—`, because it goes through fmtMoneyExact. Two renderings of the same absence, one row apart.
(2) The empty month, עסק-לדוגמה-report-2020-01.xlsx: the screen for /reports?month=2020-01 shows סה״כ חשבוניות —, מע״מ —, שולם — (out/exports/06-reports-2020-01.txt). The file writes `סה״כ לפני מע״מ`, `סה״כ מע״מ`, `סה״כ כולל מע״מ` and `הוצאה נטו` as empty money-formatted cells — but `זיכויים שקוזזו | 0 | ILS` as a literal zero, in the same block, for the same empty month.
(3) The mixed-currency month writes 0.00 for everything (EXP-01).
Why it matters beyond consistency: an empty cell in a money column is not neutral in a spreadsheet. SUM() over `הוצאה ברוטו` returns 0 for 115 products whose billed cost is unknown, which is precisely the claim the em dash exists to refuse.
repro: owner → /reports/products, widen to 2026-01-01..2026-12-31 → compare the screen's — cells with the file's cells → then /reports?month=2020-01 → export → read sheet פרטי הדוח rows 6-10.
expected: One representation of 'not measured' in an exported cell, and it is not something SUM() treats as zero.
actual: Blank, `0`, and `—` are all used for the same fact, and which one you get depends on which builder and which column.

title: The export drops the provenance caveat the screen attaches to every quantity, and states 'נרכש בפועל 0' on 74 rows whose own sources are unknown
evidence:
On screen every one of the 115 products carries, under its name, `· חלק מהשורות טרם אושרו בראיה` — 'some of these lines have not been visually confirmed' (visible in out/exports/02-products-default.png). The code that renders it calls it "Provenance, not decoration. 'Some of this rests on the supplier's word' is the difference between a number you can quote back to them and one you cannot" (src/pages/ProductPurchaseSummary.tsx:107-112). The export has twelve columns (src/pages/ProductPurchaseSummary.tsx:189-201) and none of them is that flag; `includes_invoice_only_quantity` and `includes_unevidenced_quantity` are never written. The file that leaves the building states the quantities flat.
Compounding it: in 74 of 115 rows the export writes `נרכש בפועל = 0` while `התקבל` and `חויב` on the same row are empty. The screen does the same (0 in bold, — beside it). A row cannot honestly say 'we purchased zero' while declining to say how much was received.
repro: owner → /reports/products → 2026-01-01..2026-12-31 → compare a product's on-screen sub-caption with its row in the exported xlsx; count rows where column F is 0 and column D is empty.
expected: Either the provenance flag rides the export as its own column, or the quantities it qualifies do not appear unqualified in a file sent onward. And a canonical quantity whose sources are all unknown is —, not 0.
actual: The caveat is screen-only; 74 of 115 exported rows assert a purchased quantity of 0 next to blank received and blank invoiced columns.

title: An empty month exports a file with three header-only sheets and no statement that there was nothing to report
evidence: out/exports/downloads/reports-empty-2020-01__עסק-לדוגמה-report-2020-01.xlsx, 11,733 bytes. Sheets חשבוניות, תשלומים and זיכויים each contain the two title rows and the column header row and nothing else — no 'אין חשבוניות בחודש זה' line, no note. The SCREEN for the same month is better behaved: its tables say `אין תשלומים בחודש זה` and `אין זיכויים בחודש זה` (measured on the August screen, out/exports/07-reports-aug-screen.json). An accountant opening the file cannot distinguish 'January 2020 had no activity' from 'the export was filtered wrong or failed'. The export button is enabled with no warning (measured: `{"disabled":false}`).
repro: owner → /reports?month=2020-01 → ייצוא Excel → open sheets חשבוניות / תשלומים / זיכויים.
expected: A sheet with no rows says so, the way the screen's table does.

title: Nine exceptions dated today appear inside a January-2020 report, under a banner claiming the January 2020 window
evidence:
The same empty-month file carries a fifth sheet with nine rows (חשבונית תבליני הגליל ממאי, בשר והבן #7702, …) — the current open exceptions, identical to the ones in the September and August files. Rows 1-2 of that sheet read `דוח חודשי לרו״ח — עסק לדוגמה` and `ינואר 2020 · 01.01.2020–31.01.2020 · הופק 04.09.2026, 02:39`, and the summary sheet lists `חריגים פתוחים כרגע | 9` directly beneath `חשבוניות 0 / תשלומים 0 / זיכויים 0` in a column headed `מספר רשומות`. Read down that column, the 9 looks like a January-2020 count.
Mitigation that keeps this low: the sheet is NAMED `חריגים פתוחים כרגע` — 'open right now' — so the disclosure exists, just not in the two banner rows that assert the window on every sheet.
repro: owner → /reports?month=2020-01 → ייצוא Excel → sheet חריגים פתוחים כרגע, and sheet פרטי הדוח row 17.
expected: An out-of-window block either states that it is out of window in the same place the window is asserted, or is omitted from a historical month.
actual: Nine current records sit under a January 2020 banner and are counted in the same column as the month's own record counts.

title: The expenses Excel is named for the day it was produced, not the window it covers — the PDF button beside it is named for the window
evidence:
One screen, one date range (01.01.2025 – 31.12.2026), two buttons: ייצוא Excel produced `expenses-2026-09-04.xlsx` and הורדת PDF produced `expenses-2025-01-01-2026-12-31.pdf` (out/exports/03-downloads.json). The Excel name comes from `expenses-${todayISO()}.xlsx` at src/pages/Expenses.tsx:266. Every other xlsx in the product names its window (`product-purchases-2026-01-01-2026-12-31.xlsx`, `עסק-לדוגמה-report-2026-08.xlsx`). Two exports of different periods on the same day land on the same filename and the second silently replaces the first in the Downloads folder.
The file's internal header IS correct — row 2 of every sheet reads `01.01.2025 – 31.12.2026 · הופק 04.09.2026` — so this is a naming defect, not a content one.
repro: owner → /expenses → set 01.01.2025–31.12.2026 → ייצוא Excel, then הורדת PDF → compare the two filenames.
expected: `expenses-2025-01-01-2026-12-31.xlsx`, matching its own PDF and the rest of the product.

title: The row action named 'ייצוא' leads to a screen with no export control on it
evidence: The document action menu offers `בדיקת מסמך · עיבוד מחדש · ייצוא · צפייה במקור · שיוך לחשבונית · שיוך לקבלת סחורה · הסרה עם תצוגת השפעה` (out/exports/08-doc-menu-0.png). Choosing ייצוא navigates to the document review screen for pricelist-A.csv. Enumerating every button there for /הורד|ייצוא|CSV|Excel|xlsx/i returned `[]` — no download control of any kind (out/exports/08-doc-export-modal.txt, out/exports/08-doc-export-step.png). The screen instead says `האישור זמין רק למעלה המסמך בתפקיד בעלים, משרד או ספק` — approval is limited to the document's uploader — which names the blocking condition but never mentions the export the menu item promised. The item is gated only on `snapshot?.stage` being 'review' or 'completed' (src/pages/DocumentsInbox.tsx:1019), not on whether an export is actually reachable.
repro: owner → /documents → open a document's action menu → ייצוא → enumerate the buttons on the destination.
expected: A menu item named 'export' either produces a file or explains, on arrival, what has to happen first for it to.
actual: It navigates to a review screen with no export affordance and a message about a different restriction.

title: The bank import template is an English-keyed five-column sheet with no currency column, no example row and no Hebrew at all
evidence:
out/exports/downloads/bank-template__inplace-bank-import-v1.xlsx, 16,435 bytes, one sheet 'Bank Transactions' containing exactly two rows: `INPLACE_BANK_IMPORT | 1` and `transaction_date | description | direction | amount | reference`. No data row, no instruction row, no Hebrew — reached from a Hebrew button reading `הורדת התבנית העדכנית`. `direction` expects the literal English strings 'debit'/'credit' (src/lib/bankImportWorkbook.ts:160-167) and nothing in the file says so. There is no currency column, and the parser has no notion of one, so every imported bank line carries an amount with no currency of its own.
Noted as low and possibly pre-existing: this is a static asset at public/templates/inplace-bank-import-v1.xlsx, not something this deploy rebuilt.
repro: owner → /bank → ייבוא תדפיס בנק → הורדת התבנית העדכנית → open the file.
expected: A template a Hebrew bookkeeper can fill in: labelled columns, one worked example row, and the accepted direction values stated.
actual: Two machine-readable header rows and nothing else.

title: A product name beginning with '-' gains a visible leading apostrophe in the exported file
evidence: Screen: `- ס 10מזלג ורסאי ניצוצות כסף -אר`. File: `'- ס 10מזלג ורסאי ניצוצות כסף -אר` (1 of 115 rows in product-purchases-2026-01-01-2026-12-31.xlsx). The apostrophe comes from `neutralizeSpreadsheetString` (src/lib/documentExport.ts:202-203), which prefixes any string starting `= + - @ tab CR`. Excel's apostrophe-as-text-prefix convention applies to values TYPED into the grid; a shared string written into the file is displayed verbatim, so the apostrophe is visible to the reader. An xlsx `<c t="s">` is never evaluated as a formula in the first place — the neutralizer is load-bearing for the CSV path and is mutating tenant data on the xlsx one. The right shape for xlsx is the cell's `quotePrefix` style attribute, which is not stored in the string.
repro: owner → /reports/products → 2026-01-01..2026-12-31 → export → compare the first product's name in column A with the same product on screen.
expected: The exported name is the name.
actual: An apostrophe the tenant did not type is prepended and will be visible when the file is opened.

title: RETRACTION of a prior agent's finding: /reports/products does NOT yield nothing, and the export is not dropping a column
evidence:
The prior report was '115 products, invoice_count 0, gross_amount_by_currency null everywhere, and the downloaded xlsx has 115 data rows with the gross-expense column blank in every one'. Re-measured with a reader that honours the `r=` cell reference: the file has TWELVE columns, and the one before `הוצאה ברוטו` is `עלות לפי ההזמנה` — the committed cost migration 0301 added — which is POPULATED on 115 of 115 rows (₪2,274.80, ₪792.00, ₪78.30 …). The screen shows the same twelve-column picture: committed cost populated, gross expense —. Export and screen agree exactly, row for row.
So the answer to 'is the export dropping a column the screen has': no. The report is faithfully reproducing a screen on which the BILLED figure is genuinely unknown because no approved invoice line in this tenant is matched to an order item — which is the exact condition 0301 was written to survive, and it does. The gross column being blank in every row is a true observation that supported a false conclusion.
Also retracted, mine, before it became a finding: I read the September payments sheet as missing a 600 ILS supplier row. That file had been downloaded by another agent at 00:40; a payment was recorded afterwards. A fresh export taken in the same session as the screen reconciles to it exactly — 300+262 / 300+262 / 300+300 = 1,724 ILS across three suppliers, matching the tile and the three supplier rows.
Also retracted: I briefly read money cells as carrying no number format. They carry built-in numFmtId 4 (`#,##0.00`); my reader was only resolving custom numFmts.
expected: n/a — this entry exists to withdraw a finding, not to raise one.
actual: The committed-cost column is present and populated in both the screen and the file.
